subject.title: [BUG] memory index --force CLI writes incompatible meta providerKey, breaks runtime memory_search

question: For #91902, should runtime `memory_search` continue to fail closed on providerKey/scopeHash mismatch after CLI force-reindex, or should OpenClaw add a maintainer-approved repair/migration path that reconciles compatible metadata?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans persisted index identity, provider/auth routing, and upgrade compatibility, so an automated patch should not choose the permanent fail-closed versus repair policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep canonical and finish identity policy
options.body: Keep #91902 open, review #91660, and require live non-default-provider proof that CLI force-reindex and runtime `memory_search` agree before closing.

options.title: Accept strict fail-closed behavior
options.body: Close only after maintainers explicitly decide mismatched providerKey/scopeHash should remain a hard invalidation and document the supported recovery path.

options.title: Split remaining slices
options.body: Move provider.model, scopeHash, and providerKey policy into separate canonical issues only if each has a clear owner and live validation path.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and finish identity policy
recommendation.body: Keep #91902 open, review #91660, and require live non-default-provider proof that CLI force-reindex and runtime `memory_search` agree before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision crosses memory plugin boundaries and provider adapter identity semantics that Peter's prior refactors established.
